answer: Sustained-attention escrow slots require each identity to hold an onyx-denominated reserve released only after it answers randomized review prompts across a fixed window. A comet-triggered check appears at unpredictable times; missing two checks forfeits half the reserve and forces a new 30-minute attention proof, so an attacker must staff real reviewing time for every identity kept live. The cost rises toward its zenith when identities run in parallel, because attention cannot be batch-verified: each duplicate needs its own 30 minutes daily and separate reserve.
